newsitem.title: BOSNIA: EU police to leave Mostar policing to former foes.
newsitem.headline: EU police to leave Mostar policing to former foes.

text.p: European Union police will next week leave the Bosnian city of Mostar, a town divided by bitter Moslem-Croat fighting, and hand over law and order duties to the former foes, a U.N. official said on Friday.

Robert Wasserman, deputy commissioner of the U.N. Police Task Force (IPTF) in Bosnia, said his forces would restrict themselves to monitoring Moslem-Croat police work to make sure it meets international standards.
Moslems and Croats fought a bitter 11-month war in 1993 which ended in a U.S.-sponsored agreement to form a federation in February 1994.
The agreement stopped the fighting but peace has come slowly to Mostar, a city divided into Moslem and Croat sectors, which the EU administration has been trying to reunite.
Mostar has become notorious as a haven for criminal gangs, mostly run by Croats, according to the EU.
Moslems and Croats have been patrolling the town's central area alongside EU police, but next Tuesday's planned handover would leave them on their own.

Wasserman said his men would monitor local police in the city until the end of 1996, when a joint Moslem-Croat police force is expected to be established throughout the federation territory in Bosnia.
"It is the intention to continue the work of the unified (Moslem-Croat) police force until the new federation police are established," Wasserman told reporters.
